title: Geometrical and Optical Isomerism
notes: **Geometrical isomerism (cis-trans):** restricted rotation around a double bond or ring gives different spatial arrangements. Cis: similar groups on same side. Trans: similar groups on opposite sides.

**Example â€” but-2-ene:** cis-but-2-ene has both methyl groups on same side, dipole moment non-zero, boiling point 3.7Â°C. Trans-but-2-ene has methyl groups opposite, dipole moment zero, boiling point 0.9Â°C.

**Optical isomerism:** compounds with same connectivity but different spatial arrangement around a chiral carbon (asymmetric carbon with four different groups). They rotate plane-polarized light in opposite directions.
**d-form (dextrorotatory):** rotates plane-polarized light to the right (clockwise). (+)-lactic acid.
**l-form (levorotatory):** rotates plane-polarized light to the left (anticlockwise). (âˆ’)-lactic acid.
**Racemic mixture:** equal amounts of d- and l-forms. Net rotation is zero. Can be separated by reaction with a chiral resolving agent.
